process.note: CV and a short statement, with up to three division and location choices.
Pre-recorded answers to competency and motivation questions, about two minutes each.
Some divisions run a 30 minute phone or video screen before the final round.
Two to four back-to-back interviews with associates, VPs and MDs, mixing technical, CV and fit questions.
Usually a phone call within a week or two, then a written contract.

questions.question: Why Goldman Sachs over another bank?
questions.whyTheyAsk: They want to see you chose them for a reason, not because they are famous.
questions.prepTip: Name one deal, team or value of the firm and link it to something you have actually done.

questions.question: Walk me through a DCF.
questions.whyTheyAsk: It checks you understand how a company is valued, step by step.
questions.prepTip: Practise a two minute version: cash flows, discount rate, terminal value, enterprise to equity value.

questions.question: Tell me about a time you worked in a team that disagreed.
questions.whyTheyAsk: Banking teams work long hours together, so they check how you handle friction.
questions.prepTip: Use STAR and say what you personally did to move the team forward.

questions.question: Pitch me a stock.
questions.whyTheyAsk: It shows whether you follow markets and can argue a view clearly.
questions.prepTip: Pick one company you know well, give two reasons and one risk, and keep it under two minutes.

questions.question: What is a recent deal Goldman worked on that interested you?
questions.whyTheyAsk: They test whether you follow the firm and the market, not just the brand.
questions.prepTip: Read the firm's recent press releases and be ready to explain why the deal made sense for the client.

questions.question: Describe a goal you reached that others thought you could not.
questions.whyTheyAsk: It checks drive and how you respond to doubt.
questions.prepTip: Choose a real, specific goal and be clear about the obstacle and the result.

questions.question: How would you value a company with no profits yet?
questions.whyTheyAsk: It checks you can adapt standard valuation methods.
questions.prepTip: Mention revenue multiples and comparable companies, and say why a DCF is harder here.

questions.question: Tell me about a mistake you made and what you learnt.
questions.whyTheyAsk: They want honesty and evidence that you learn quickly.
questions.prepTip: Pick a real but recoverable mistake and spend most of the answer on what changed afterwards.

questions.question: Where do you see interest rates going over the next year, and how would that affect M&A?
questions.whyTheyAsk: It tests commercial awareness and linking macro news to the business.
questions.prepTip: Have one view with a reason, and explain how financing costs change deal activity.

questions.question: Why investment banking rather than consulting?
questions.whyTheyAsk: They check you understand the job and will stay with it.
questions.prepTip: Talk about the transaction work itself and something concrete that drew you to it.

tips: Practise HireVue answers on camera: you get one attempt and a short time to think.
Read the Financial Times for the week before your superday and have two market stories ready.
Expect every interviewer to ask 'why Goldman': have a specific answer, not a general one.
Know every line of your CV well enough to talk about it for two minutes.
